slides.text: Never buy a four-dollar Vitamix from an estate sale where the previous owner is described simply as 'The Crone of Maple Street.' The first morning I plugged it in to make a protein shake, the speed dial glowed blood-red and a guttural voice echoed from the blades: 'FEED ME THE FLESH OF THE INNOCENT.' I was already twenty minutes late for work, so I tossed in half a frozen banana and a scoop of whey.

The blender shrieked in eldritch fury, spun at Mach 3, and produced the most velvety, micro-aerated peanut-butter banana smoothie I have ever tasted in my life. Zero ice chunks. The next morning, it demanded 'THE STILL-BEATING HEART OF A USURER.' I offered it kale, chia seeds, and a splash of almond milk. It grumbled in Latin about my lack of ambition, then emulsified the kale so smoothly it tasted like gelato.

We have an arrangement now. Every Sunday, I prick my thumb on a rose thorn to give the motor housing a tiny drop of mortal blood, and in exchange, it makes me a Michelin-starred gazpacho and crushes ice without waking my neighbors. My cholesterol is down thirty points, my skin is glowing, and honestly, the dark lord of kitchen appliances is way less needy than my Nespresso machine.
